name: Danby DCR032C1WDB 3.2 cu ft compact refrigerator
sourceNote: Danby lists 115 V, 66.4 W, and 218 kWh/year. Average draw is 218 × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = 24.9 W. Duty cycle 0.375 is that average divided by 66.4 W, so it is an annual-average compressor fraction, not a hot-day measurement. Startup watts are not published.

name: Danby DAR032B1SLM 3.2 cu ft compact refrigerator
sourceNote: Danby lists 115 V, 150 W, and 259 kWh/year. Average draw is 29.6 W. Duty cycle 0.197 is the annual average implied by those two figures. Startup watts are not published.

sourceNote: Danby lists 115 V, 90 W, and 253 kWh/year. Average draw is 28.9 W. Duty cycle 0.321 is the annual average implied by those two figures. Startup watts are not published.

name: Danby DAR010A1BDB 1.0 cu ft compact refrigerator
sourceNote: Danby lists 115 V, 90 W, and 241 kWh/year. Average draw is 27.5 W. Duty cycle 0.306 is the annual average implied by those two figures. Startup watts are not published.

name: Samsung RT18DG6300 17.5 cu ft top-freezer refrigerator
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 333 kWh/year for RT18DG6300**, a 17.5 cu ft top freezer with no ice maker. Average draw is 333 × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = 38.0 W. Compressor running watts and startup watts are not in the listing, so Willrun will not issue a runs or won't-run verdict.

name: Whirlpool WZC3209LW 9 cu ft chest freezer

name: Danby DCF100A5WDB 10 cu ft chest freezer
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 211 kWh/year for this 10.0 cu ft manual-defrost chest freezer. Average draw is 24.1 W. Running and startup watts are not in the listing, so there is no run verdict.

name: Frigidaire FFFH20F3W 20 cu ft upright freezer
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 478 kWh/year for FFFH20F3W*, a 20.0 cu ft upright freezer. Average draw is 54.6 W. Running and startup watts are not in the listing, so there is no run verdict.

name: BLACK+DECKER BDM05C 5,000 Btu/h window air conditioner
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 5,000 Btu/h, CEER 14.4, 115 V, variable-speed compressor, and 260.4 kWh/year. Rated input is 5,000 ÷ 14.4 = 347.2 W. That matches the listed annual energy at the DOE room-AC assumption of 750 hours (347.2 × 750 ÷ 1,000 = 260.4). The 347.2 W figure is the draw while cooling at the rated condition, not a whole-year average. Startup watts are not published.

name: BLACK+DECKER BD08NWES 8,000 Btu/h window air conditioner
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 8,000 Btu/h, CEER 15, 115 V, variable-speed compressor, and 400 kWh/year. Rated input is 8,000 ÷ 15 = 533.3 W, which matches 400 kWh at 750 hours. Startup watts are not published.

name: BLACK+DECKER BD12NWES 12,000 Btu/h window air conditioner
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 12,000 Btu/h, CEER 15, 115 V, variable-speed compressor, and 600 kWh/year. Rated input is 12,000 ÷ 15 = 800 W, which matches 600 kWh at 750 hours. Startup watts are not published.

name: GE PWJV10 10,000 Btu/h window air conditioner
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists model PWJV10W**# at 10,000 Btu/h, CEER 16, and 468.8 kWh/year, with a variable-speed compressor. Rated input is 10,000 ÷ 16 = 625 W. 625 × 750 ÷ 1,000 = 468.75, which rounds to the listed 468.8 kWh. Startup watts are not published.

name: Zoeller Model 53 3/10 HP sump pump, 115 V
sourceNote: Zoeller lists the Model 53 at 3/10 HP, 115 V or 230 V, and 4.8–9.7 A. The 115 V automatic model in Zoeller's 50-series technical table is 9.7 A. Running watts used here are 9.7 × 115 = 1,115.5 W. Startup amps are not published. How often the float runs is site-specific, so no duty cycle is stored.

name: ResMed AirSense 11, typical power from the user guide
sourceNote: Americas user guide, 65 W power supply section: typical power consumption 56.1 W (111.5 VA) and peak power consumption 73.2 W (137.6 VA). This is the published system figure, not the lower no-humidifier row on ResMed's separate therapy-power sheet.

name: ResMed AirSense 11 AutoSet, no humidifier
sourceNote: ResMed's therapy-device power table lists AirSense 11 AutoSet operation at 7 Wh and standby at 2 Wh. The operation figure is energy per hour, so the average draw is 7 W. ResMed notes the values were measured in a lab and that a local meter can differ.

name: ResMed AirSense 11 with HumidAir 11 and ClimateLineAir 11
sourceNote: The same ResMed table lists AirSense 11 AutoSet with HumidAir 11 and heated ClimateLineAir 11 at 55 Wh during operation. Average draw is 55 W.

name: ResMed AirMini travel CPAP
sourceNote: ResMed's table lists AirMini operation at 6.3 Wh and standby at 1 Wh. Average draw during operation is 6.3 W.

name: LG 55QNED85 55-inch TV
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR on-mode power for 55QNED85TU* is 76.9 W at a 54.6-inch viewable diagonal. Standby with the network disconnected is 0.30 W. On-mode power is what the station has to supply while the TV is on.

name: Sansui LE-32T1 32-inch TV
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR on-mode power for Sansui LE-32T1 is 28.4 W at a 31.5-inch viewable diagonal.

name: Sansui LE-55V4 55-inch TV

name: Samsung QN65QN90D 65-inch TV
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR on-mode power for QN65QN90DAF is 121.96 W at a 64.5-inch viewable diagonal. Standby with the network disconnected is 0.30 W. Stored running watts are rounded to 122.

name: LG 27BA450 27-inch monitor
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR certified displays lists LG 27BA450 at 11.80 W on-mode and 0.14 W sleep, 27-inch screen.

name: Amana AMND501BW dehumidifier, about 50 pints/day
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 49.43 pints/day, integrated energy factor 2.01 L/kWh, and 520 kWh/year. Operating draw at the rated test condition is (49.43 × 0.473176 L/pint ÷ 24 h) ÷ 2.01 L/kWh × 1,000 = 485 W. That is the draw while it is removing water at the rated rate, not a whole-year average. Startup watts are not published.

name: Frigidaire FHDD2233Y1 dehumidifier, about 22 pints/day
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 22.27 pints/day, integrated energy factor 1.70 L/kWh, and 276 kWh/year. Operating draw at the rated test condition is (22.27 × 0.473176 ÷ 24) ÷ 1.70 × 1,000 = 258 W. Startup watts are not published.

name: Hunter 52774 44-inch ceiling fan, high speed
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists high speed at 12.5 W, low speed at 1.6 W, and standby at 0.3 W for this 44-inch fan. The run check uses high speed. Startup watts are not published.

name: Hunter 52881 44-inch ceiling fan, high speed
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists high speed at 17.6 W, low speed at 2.7 W, and standby at 0.5 W for this 44-inch fan. Startup watts are not published.

sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists 70 CFM and 4 CFM/W. Draw is 70 ÷ 4 = 17.5 W. Startup watts are not published.

sourceNote: ENERGY STAR connected-bulb listing: 9 W, 800 lumens, 60 W equivalency.

sourceNote: Apple's MacBook Air specs page lists a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W max for the 13-inch model, and a 53.8 Wh battery. 60 W is the adapter ceiling, not a measured average workload, so the runtime is a short estimate. Some configurations on the same page ship a 35 W dual USB-C adapter instead.

name: Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe 15AKP12, ENERGY STAR short idle
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR computers v9 lists short idle at 6.1 W and sleep at 0.6 W. Short idle is not a video-call or compile load. A heavier workload was not published, so this runtime only covers idle.

sourceNote: ENERGY STAR computers v9 lists short idle at 3.8 W and sleep at 0.4 W. This is idle only.

sourceNote: ENERGY STAR computers v9 lists model A3546 short idle at 7.0 W, long idle at 5.9 W, and sleep at 0.9 W. Full compute load was not published.

name: Lasko 755320 ceramic heater, high
sourceNote: Lasko lists 120 V, current 7.5 A to 12.5 A, and energy output 900 W to 1,500 W. High is 1,500 W. A resistive element does not have a separate motor surge, so surge is set equal to the high setting. The thermostat cycles in real rooms; this entry assumes the high element is on.

name: Lasko 755320 ceramic heater, low
sourceNote: Same Lasko listing: energy output 900 W to 1,500 W. Low is the 900 W end of that range. 7.5 A × 120 V = 900 W.

name: Panasonic NN-SU656WAWH microwave, electrical input
sourceNote: Panasonic lists power supply 120 V / 60 Hz, microwave output 1,100 W, and microwave power consumption 1,500 W. The station has to supply the 1,500 W input, not the 1,100 W cooking output. A separate startup surge is not published. X-Boost and Power Lifting are not applied, because those modes are described for simple heating loads and a microwave is an electronic supply.

name: TP-Link Archer AX73 router, networked standby
sourceNote: TP-Link lists typical power consumption in networked standby, with all wired ports connected and all wireless radios activated, at 8.7 W. The power adapter is 12 V, 2.5 A, which is a supply rating and is not used as the draw.

name: LG LCE3010 induction cooktop, 1,200 W zone
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR residential electric cooking lists zone 1 at 1,200 W and zone 2 at 1,900 W for LCE3010SBE. This entry is zone 1 alone. Induction supplies are not marked eligible for X-Boost or Power Lifting, which makers describe for simple heaters.

name: LG LCE3010 induction cooktop, 1,900 W zone
sourceNote: ENERGY STAR lists zone 2 of LCE3010SBE at 1,900 W. This entry is that zone alone, not two zones together.
